---
title: "Matrix input and grading"
---

Use `matrix([a,b],[c,d])` to write a matrix in author expressions. A matrix is
different from a nested list. It must be rectangular, have at least one row
and column, and contain a value in every cell. Each dimension is at most 16,
with at most 64 entries overall. Cells contain supported scalar expressions,
not lists, equations or logical statements.

`AlgEquiv` compares dimensions and corresponding entries, `SameType` checks
matrix type, and `EqualComAss` also checks the written form of entries. Those
are the supported native STACK matrix tests here. For a question asking for
**any** basis or a matrix satisfying conditions, choose the Python-only
`IsBasis` or `MatrixProperty` test described in [Python answer tests](python-checker-api.qmd).

Use a normal `<input><type>matrix</type>...` for a fixed-size editor; it takes
its shape from the input model answer. To let learners choose the number of
vectors, add this STACK SymPy input setting, as in [the basis
examples](../examples.qmd#a-basis-for-the-null-space-of-b):

```xml
<matrix>
  <rows initial="3" min="3" max="3" resizable="0"/>
  <cols initial="1" min="1" max="3" resizable="1"/>
</matrix>
```

Each axis requires all four attributes; a fixed axis has `resizable="0"` and
equal `initial`, `min`, and `max`. The product of the two maxima must not exceed
64. The `<matrix>` sizing setting is specific to STACK SymPy and needs
adaptation for a native Moodle STACK question.

Raw cells such as `x+x`, `0.1` and `1/2` remain unchanged in the editor.
Empty cells remain invalid; resizing never inserts numerical zeros. Surviving
cells retain their raw values when resized. Validation shows the interpreted
matrix before checking.

Editing, resizing, resetting and changing variants clear previous validation,
grading and AI-feedback evidence. Reset restores the initial dimensions and
blank cells. After an `IsBasis` check, the editor can color proposed vectors;
the authored PRTs remain the only source of awarded marks.

The editor is configured through the question XML. Its reusable component and
provenance are recorded in the project source tree.

## Decisions for a question author

Choose the mathematical task before choosing a matrix answer test. `AlgEquiv`
compares a particular matrix entry by entry; it is unsuitable for “give any
basis” or “give any matrix satisfying these conditions.” Use the documented
Python-only IsBasis or MatrixProperty tests for those tasks, or supply an
equivalent custom checker in native STACK. Do not replace a family of valid
answers by equality with one convenient model answer.

Choose fixed dimensions when the shape is given. If the number of basis
vectors is part of the answer, use bounded learner-selected columns for null
and column spaces or rows for row spaces. Use the original matrix in the PRT
teacher answer, and `nullspace_basis(A)`, `columnspace_basis(A)` or
`rowspace_basis(A)` for the input model. Blank cells are invalid, and this port
cannot represent an empty basis with a zero-column matrix. Make sure the model
and authored qtests fit the configured dimensions; the build checks this.

Specify the allowed number domain: the native-compatible matrix tests inherit
the supported scalar rules, while the built-in `IsBasis` and `MatrixProperty`
tests require bounded exact rational arithmetic. An author-supplied
`PythonChecker` can define another domain within the input limits. Decide
partial credit explicitly in the
PRTs. Native matrix comparison does not automatically award credit for correct
cells, and green basis vectors do not by themselves earn part marks. Review
wrong shapes, dependent and incomplete families, alternative correct answers,
and written-form or decimal-sensitive cases before publishing.
